messages:
maria: Heads-up — UmbraTech POC kickoff. They're on RivalAPI and want behavior parity for a few weird edge cases: 'no-answer' responses (empty string vs null), function-calling shapes, and exact streaming chunk termination. They also asked about pricing for ~500k tokens/month and a short dedicated latency SLO. Can SEs confirm approach?
kevin: noted. main risks: RivalAPI returns an empty string for noop completions while many clients interpret null differently. We can normalize in an adapter but it may change eval pass/fail. also their detokenization handles escaped unicode differently.
sophia: For the empty vs null case we can add a config flag normalize_empty_response=true that converts empty->null or vice versa. Need to know which direction they expect. Also we can emulate tokenization by replaying RivalAPI's tokenizer for acceptance tests.
maria: Customer can't change their client for the POC — they want our shim to mirror RivalAPI semantics exactly (including the exact final streaming sentinel). Is that doable without breaking our metrics?
sophia: Yes — we can implement a "compat_mode" that maps frames. Our streaming currently includes metadata frames; compat_mode can strip metadata and emit plain SSE text frames plus their exact termination token (e.g., `data: [DONE]`). Small CPU/encode overhead but trivial for POC volume.
kevin: Good. Perf note: removing metadata slightly reduces payload size but adds re-encode CPU. We'll include perf regression test. Also watch out for rate limit behavior — RivalAPI returns 429 with a Retry-After (seconds). Our infra uses token-bucket with jitter; adapter will need to translate 429->429 and preserve Retry-After header.
alex-security: Quick security Qs from their compliance team: 1) Will adapter persist original requests or trimmed responses? 2) Can we disable any long-term request logs for this customer? 3) Is custom shim covered by existing SOC2 controls?
sophia: We can disable request-body logs per-instance and enable response-only short-term traces. We have a masking pipeline that can strip PII before any persistent store. Shim code will run in tenant-scoped container; it inherits our SOC2 boundary. I'll document exact controls.
maria: Commercial: They asked for a 3-month POC discount. Ask: 50% on hosted token rates vs a short-term dedicated pool. Thoughts?
kevin: Recommend hosted with a targeted 30% POC discount + engineering credits for the adapter work. Dedicated commit for 3 months is heavier operationally. If they need strict SLO, we can offer a small reserved burst pool as an add-on.
numbot-deploy: trigger: created POC environment p-umbra-001 in us-west. console: https://console.redwood.example/p/p-umbra-001
maria: Action items: @kevin prototype adapter that normalizes empty/null behavior and preserves RivalAPI streaming sentinel by Tues; @sophia confirm streaming "data: [DONE]" termination exact bytes and add ops doc + masking SLA; @alex-security produce short Q&A for their compliance ask about logs and SOC2 scope. I'll prepare a slim term sheet once we have perf numbers.
kevin: Ack. I'll also run a token-compat test set to check detokenization differences and surface examples where outputs shift semantics.
kevin: Quick test snippet for replay:
```bash
# capture RivalAPI streaming sample (SSE)
curl -N https://api.rival.example/v1/stream -H \"Authorization: Bearer RIVAL_TOKEN\" -o rival.stream
# replay via shim to validate client-facing behavior
curl -N https://p-umbra-001.internal/s/compat -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_TEST\" --data-binary @rival.stream
```
sophia: We'll add an automated CI test asserting the final SSE frame equals exactly `data: [DONE]` (including newline sequence). Also add config toggle: compat_mode: rivalapi_v1. Ops will expose a runtime flag to avoid redeploy.
maria: If UmbraTech's validator is strict about escaped Unicode (e.g., "\u2019" vs real char), we may need to add a detokenizer shim step. Ping me if they ask for token-level diffs.
kevin: Will do. Scheduling: demo Wed 10am PT. I'll put together a short checklist for the customer-facing demo: sample prompt set, streaming test, null/empty normalization, and pricing slide.
maria: Thanks — keep the thread updated.
